## Policies

### Peer Review

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Type** | Double-anonymous: "Neither author nor reviewers know the identity of each other"; manuscripts are first assessed by an editor and, if sent out, the process "usually" involves at least two referees (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/peer-review-information/review-process; retrieved 2026-11-23). Authors must not allude to themselves as authors anywhere in the text, including in citations (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Transferable / Cascade?** | Blank. The review-process page read (2026-11-23) mentions no transfer scheme |
| **Reviewer reports published?** | Blank. Nothing found on the pages read |
| **Typical R+R rounds** | SciRev, n = 13: 1.1 rounds on average (https://scirev.org/journal/british-journal-of-political-science/, 2026-11-23) |
| **Reviewer recommendations** | Blank. No instruction on suggested reviewers found. Appeals: contact the Editor with the reason; the appeal is reviewed by the Editor and another team member not involved in the review, and the Editor decides (review-process page) |

### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | Yes, a dedicated "Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) Tools" section in the author instructions (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials; retrieved 2026-11-23), plus a second statement in the acknowledgements guidance |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | No gate found. Use is allowed with declaration |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 (allowed with mandatory declaration; the acknowledgements guidance warns that failure to acknowledge AI assistance "may lead to disqualification of the paper") |
| **Summary** | AI tools cannot be listed as authors. Declare and describe any use of an AI tool to generate text or images (translation included) or to analyse or extract insights from data; minimal non-generative uses (spelling or language checks, single words or brief phrases, minor formatting) need no declaration. Declaration goes in an acknowledgments section or footnote (text), the methods section (data analysis) or figure captions (images), with tool name and version, dates, how it was used. The acknowledgements guidance separately says assistance from writing agencies, language editors or AI tools must be noted in the cover letter and in the Acknowledgements. Retrieved 2026-11-23 |
| **Source URL** | https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials |

### Preprint Policy

> Journal-level statement: this journal "allows preprints to be posted anywhere at any time, including before submission" (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/journal-policies/open-access-options, retrieved 2026-11-23). The prior-publication policy adds that a preprint on a personal website, institutional repository or preprint archive is not prior or duplicate publication (preparing-your-materials page). Review is double-anonymous, and the pages do not discuss whether a posted preprint conflicts with anonymity.

| Stage | Allowed? | Notes |
|-------|----------|-------|
| Pre-submission | Yes | Per the statements above |
| Under review | Yes | "At any time"; no separate under-review rule found |
| Post-acceptance (AAM) | Yes, conditions on the publisher page | The journal is fully Gold OA, so the accepted version is published openly; the Green OA spreadsheet the page links to was not read |
| Version of Record | Open access under a Creative Commons licence | Authors may choose any of the six CC licences (open-access-options page) |

## Format

> Source for the rules below: the journal's "Preparing your materials" page, https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials (retrieved 2026-11-23), unless another page is named.

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Article types accepted** | Research Article, Letter and Comment (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/instructions-contributors). Comments respond to BJPolS research articles or letters and "on occasion" are published; no APC applies to them. Authors indicate the category when submitting |
| **Word limit** | Research Articles "generally" 4,000 to 10,000 words, with articles above 10,000 considered "only in exceptional circumstances"; Letters up to 4,000 words. All parts of the manuscript count except the appendix and the bibliography, so captions and footnotes count (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Word limit negotiability** | Partly stated: the 10,000-word ceiling is worded as an exception route ("exceptional circumstances"); no procedure for requesting one is described |
| **Abstract limit** | An abstract of no more than 150 words for all article types, with 5 to 7 keywords. Median abstract length among the 495 Crossref records that have one: 149 words, maximum 321 (computed 2026-11-23) |
| **Reference limit** | No cap found; the bibliography is excluded from the word count. "Cambridge A" style, in-text author-date references with page numbers for quotations (for example "Elster 1983, 174"); "et al." for three or more authors |
| **Supplementary material** | Supplementary material may be hosted on the Cambridge platform and is a formal part of the record; appendices at the back of the typeset article are allowed for material essential to understanding; replication materials for quantitative data go to the BJPolS Dataverse (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Figure/Table limits** | No count limit found. Tables should fit 190 x 120 mm and figures 200 x 133 mm at 300 dpi or more; colour is published at no additional charge; each placed in the text near where discussed |
| **Style / submission format** | Double spacing, 12-point or larger type, left margin at least 25 mm and right margin at least 40 mm; Word or LaTeX (LaTeX with source files); optional Overleaf template; either English or American spelling if consistent; "-ize" preferred; gender-neutral language expected; Editorial Manager submission (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/author-instructions/submitting-your-materials); ORCID required for corresponding authors; manuscripts are run through plagiarism detection |

### Orientation

> Counts below come from Crossref records of this journal dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (541 journal-article records, of which 495 = 91.5% carry an abstract), matched in title plus abstract (case-insensitive, word-boundary regexes; exact regexes under AI-Research Notes). | Dimension | Assessment |

| **Empirical vs. Theoretical** | Empirical designs dominate by keyword count: survey terms 203 (41.0%), experiment-type terms 160 (32.3%), causal-identification terms 61 (12.3%), against normative or political-theory terms 17 (3.4%) and formal-model terms 8 (1.6%) of 495. The journal says it is "committed to no methodological orthodoxy" beyond logical and mathematical validity and appropriate evidence (preparing-your-materials page) |
| **Quantitative vs. Qualitative** | The word "quantitative" appears in 14 records (2.8%) and "qualitative" in 11 (2.2%); interviews in 13 (2.6%); case study or process tracing in 8 (1.6%); mixed-methods terms in 4 (0.8%). Quantitative designs are named by method rather than by the word "quantitative" |
| **Cross-disciplinary openness** | The aims text says articles from scholars in related disciplines (sociology, social psychology, economics and philosophy) "appear frequently" and that contributions are invited in all fields of political science and political theory "except the history of political thought" (preparing-your-materials page) |

The journal states no political position on any page read |

### Framing Requirements

- **Mandatory framing?** A scope statement rather than a framing rule: "Innovative and authoritative work addressed to problems of general significance to students of politics will be published whatever the period(s) or place(s) drawn upon for evidence" (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **What kind of engagement?** Contributions are invited in all fields of political science and political theory, except the history of political thought (same page). The journal says it is committed to "no methodological orthodoxy" other than clear use of words, logical and mathematical validity and appropriate evidence for empirical statements.
- **Article type and length**: Research Article (generally 4,000 to 10,000 words), Letter (up to 4,000 words, described as "making a big point shortly and succinctly") and Comment, with a 150-word abstract and 5 to 7 keywords (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/instructions-contributors and the preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23).
- **Editorial discretion**: the Editors "reserve the right to decline articles" judged inconsistent with editorial policy (preparing-your-materials page). The review-process page says manuscripts are first assessed by an editor before any referee is asked (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/peer-review-information/review-process).
- **Consequences of ignoring it**: Blank. No source states what share of rejections is for scope, and no desk-rejection statistics were found.

### Methodological Preferences

> Counts are Crossref records of this journal dated 2021-01-01 to 2026-11-23 (541 journal-article records; 495 with an abstract) whose title or abstract matches the regex listed under AI-Research Notes. Shares use 495 as the denominator. Scoring convention of this research pass (its own, not an external standard): share 0 = 0; under 1% = 1; 1-5% = 2; over 5% = 3; a 4-5 only with a cited editorial statement. Scores measure how often a method appears, not how a reviewer would judge it. No 4-5 is assigned: the journal's pluralism statement (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/author-instructions/preparing-your-materials) welcomes all traditions without ranking methods. Rows for political-science practice are added where the schema's rows do not fit.

| Method | Receptiveness (0-5) | Evidence |
|--------|---------------------|----------|
| Quantitative experimental | 3 | Experiment, randomized, field-experiment or survey-experiment terms 160 (32.3%) of 495 (regex `experiment`). The instructions "encourage pre-registration" and prefer OSF or EGAP registrations; pre-registration terms appear in 23 records (4.6%, regex `preregistration`) (preparing-your-materials page) |
| Quantitative observational / causal inference (added row) | 3 | Causal-identification terms 61 (12.3%) (regex `causal_identification`); survey, panel-data, cross-national or public-opinion terms 203 (41.0%) (regex `survey_data`). Authors of accepted articles with quantitative data must deposit data, codebook, run files and output on the BJPolS Dataverse; articles are held at copy-editing until the check is done (preparing-your-materials page) |
| Qualitative interviews | 2 | `interviews?` 13 (2.6%), the word "qualitative" 11 (2.2%) of 495. The journal says it takes "a flexible approach to data sharing and transparency" for non-quantitative traditions (preparing-your-materials page) |
| Qualitative case studies (added row) | 2 | Case-study, process-tracing, comparative-historical or within-case terms 8 (1.6%) (regex `case_study`) |
| Autoethnography | 0 | Does not fit political science as a named method: 0 of 495 records match `auto-?ethnograph`, and 0 match `ethnograph`. The row is kept for schema parity |
| Theoretical / Conceptual (normative theory) | 2 | Normative, political-theory, political-philosophy, democratic-theory or theories-of-justice terms 17 (3.4%) (regex `normative_theory`). The journal invites political theory except the history of political thought (preparing-your-materials page); "Political Philosophy and Ethics" is the primary topic of 12 works and "Political Theory and Democracy" of 22 (OpenAlex, 2021-2026) |
| Formal theory (added row) | 2 | Formal-model, formal-theory, game-theory, equilibrium, signaling-game, bargaining-model or theoretical-model terms 8 (1.6%) (regex `formal_model`; narrow, so a lower bound). The aims text names "logical and mathematical validity" among its canons |
| Mixed methods | 1 | Mixed-methods, multimethod or nested-analysis terms 4 (0.8%) (regex `mixed_methods`) |
| Meta-analysis / systematic review | 2 | Meta-analysis or systematic-review terms 5 (1.0%, 5 of 495 = 1.01%) (regex `meta_sr_only`); replication, reappraisal or registered-report terms 11 (2.2%) (regex `meta_replication`). Not a listed article type |

### Practical Concerns

| Concern | Detail |
|---------|--------|
| **IRB requirement strictness** | An ethical statement is "optional" in the list of end-of-manuscript statements (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/author-instructions/submitting-your-materials, retrieved 2026-11-23). The instructions point to the publisher's publishing ethics policies and state authorship and affiliation rules (preparing-your-materials page). No human-subjects review requirement specific to this journal was found on the pages read |
| **Single-author acceptance** | Single-author records are 131 of 509 Crossref records with author lists (25.7%) for 2021-2026 (retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Independent scholar friendliness** | Blank. The affiliation rule says affiliations should be the institution(s) at which the research was conducted, supported or approved; nothing on independent scholars (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23; searched the instruction pages for "independent scholar" and "unaffiliated" with no match) |
| **Data transparency requirement** | Strict for quantitative data: authors of accepted articles must deposit data, codebook, run files and log files on the BJPolS Dataverse (https://dataverse.harvard.edu/dataverse/BJPolS); exceptions for restricted-access source data are considered but "the strong presumption will be against" them; the journal says it takes a flexible approach for sensitive human-subject data and non-quantitative work (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23). A Data Availability Statement is encouraged, and the research-transparency page confirms the DA-RT signatory status (https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/british-journal-of-political-science/information/journal-policies/research-transparency) |
| **OPSEC compatibility** | Double-anonymous; authors must not identify themselves in text or references (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23). Preprints may be posted at any time (open-access-options page), which can reveal authorship. A competing-interests declaration is required in the submission; the funding declaration is required if applicable |
| **AI use** | Declaration required for generative use that produces text or images or analyses data; AI cannot be an author; unacknowledged assistance may lead to disqualification (preparing-your-materials page, retrieved 2026-11-23) |
| **Open access and cost** | Fully open access since 2025; APC GBP 2,610 or USD 3,655, with institutional agreements, equity initiatives and discount or waiver requests after acceptance (fees-and-pricing and open-access-options pages, retrieved 2026-11-23) |

## Strategic Notes

> Each statement below follows from a fact recorded above and names it. Where the evidence does not support a statement, the field says so.

### Hard Blockers

- **Length**: research articles generally 4,000 to 10,000 words excluding bibliography and appendix, with more only in exceptional circumstances; letters up to 4,000 (Format).
- **Anonymity**: authors must not identify themselves anywhere in text or references (Peer Review; preparing-your-materials page).
- **Data and code**: authors of accepted articles with quantitative data must deposit data, codebook, run and log files on the BJPolS Dataverse, and articles are held until that is checked; exceptions face a "strong presumption" against (Data transparency requirement).
- **Scope**: the history of political thought is excluded from the invitation (Framing Requirements).
- **AI use**: undeclared AI assistance in drafting "may lead to disqualification of the paper" (AI Policy).

### Soft Tax

- **Time**: the only figures are SciRev, n = 13: 3.1 months for the first review round and 5.9 months in total for accepted manuscripts; no editor-reported figure was found (Review Cycle Time).
- **Cost**: Gold OA is the only route and the APC is GBP 2,610 or USD 3,655 unless an institutional agreement, equity scheme, waiver or discount applies (Open Access).
- **Preprints and anonymity**: preprints are allowed at any time but can reveal authorship under double-anonymous review (Preprint Policy, Practical Concerns).
- **Selectivity**: unknown; no acceptance or desk-rejection statistics were found (Metrics).

### Best Suited For

- Empirical comparative or behavioural work with survey, experimental or causal designs: those terms appear in 41.0%, 32.3% and 12.3% of 495 abstracts (Methodological Preferences).
- Short, pointed contributions: the Letter category (up to 4,000 words) exists for "a big point shortly and succinctly" (Format; Framing Requirements).
- Articles that range across countries and fields: the aims text names a wide range of countries and specialisms and frequent contributions from neighbouring disciplines (Orientation; Epistemological & Political Leanings).
- Open-access publication with funding routes: fully Gold OA with institutional, equity and waiver routes (Open Access).

### Not Recommended For

- Work in the history of political thought: excluded from the invitation (Framing Requirements).
- Authors needing a verified acceptance or turnaround figure before choosing: none was found (Metrics; Review Cycle Time).
- Authors who cannot share quantitative data and code: strong presumption against exceptions (Practical Concerns).
- Authors who cannot afford to leave identity unmarked in a preprint: double-anonymous review and preprint-at-any-time can conflict, and the pages do not say how the journal treats it (Preprint Policy).
